studyMetadata.title: Text, Visual, Embodied Learning Study: Summer 2026

response.prompt:
## Homework Assignment

**Description:** In this survey, you will learn about confidence intervals through a series of instructional videos and guided self-exploration activities.

To ensure a smooth experience, please:

- Find a quiet environment free from distractions.
- Use a device with a stable internet connection. **Please use a computer/laptop for this activity**; otherwise some of the functions will not work properly.
- Make sure your audio is working properly.

You are completing this survey to receive extra credit for your course.

**<u>The survey will take approximately one hour, and must be completed in a single sitting.</u>**

Although credit is based on completion, **<u>you must remain engaged and complete all components as intended in order to receive extra credit.</u>** Even if you don't know the answer to a question, we'd like to see your thinking process. For example, if you answer "yes" or "I'm not sure" for all questions you will not get credit. AI use is also prohibited in this survey.

Please advance the page if you agree to share your data anonymously with the research team. You may leave the page now if you do not wish to participate.
Are you in a quiet environment, using a computer or laptop for this activity, and do you expect to be able to devote your full attention to it for the next hour?
options: No. I will come back to the survey.

response.prompt: If you encounter an open-response question in this survey and you are not sure of the answer, what should you do?
options: Leave the question blank because I do not know the correct answer.
Write “I don’t know” and move on without further explanation.
Take my best guess and explain my thinking, even if I am unsure, by describing what I know, what I am considering, or where I feel confused.
Search online or ask someone else for the answer.

response.prompt: The next set of questions tests your knowledge prior to the instruction. Try to give your best guess and reasoning if you are unsure about a question.
What is a sampling distribution?
options: The distribution of data values within a single sample.
The distribution of all possible sample statistics (e.g., means) from repeated random samples of the same size from a population.
The distribution of the population statistics (e.g., means) based on the sample statistic we observed.
The distribution of errors that occur when sampling.

response.prompt:
What does the shaded area represent in the sampling distribution below? **[Select ALL that apply]**

![Sampling Distribution of the Mean](tve-learning-summer/assets/samplingDist.png)
options: The probability that the population mean falls in between 95 and 105.
The probability that a sample mean will fall in between 95 and 105.
The sample means that are not unlikely to come from a population with a mean of 100.
The sample means that are unlikely to come from a population with a mean of 100.

response.prompt: Suppose the sampling distribution of sample means is centered at 3. What does that mean?
options: The true population mean is assumed to be 3

response.prompt: If the sampling distribution of the sample means were centered at a different location on the horizontal axis, what would be different?
options: The variability of individual scores changes

response.prompt: If the sampling distribution of sample means were centered at a different location such that the center of the distribution gets closer to 5.5, the likelihood of observing a sample mean of 5.5 from this sampling distribution ___________.
In your own words, what is a 95% confidence interval? What information does it provide?

Using sample mean = 4, standard error = 2, construct a 95% confidence interval using a z score of 1.96.

You do not have to do the calculation, just plug in the numbers in the equation.
Lower bound:
Upper bound:
What is the margin of error?
options: The maximum difference between the sample mean and the population mean.
The range of possible values for the population parameter.
The amount added and subtracted from the sample statistic, usually based on the standard error and a critical value.
The standard deviation of the sample data.

response.prompt: If we change our confidence level from 95% to 99%, how does the change affect the width of the confidence interval?
options: The width of the CI will become wider
The width of the CI will become narrower
The width of the CI will not change

response.prompt: In your own words, what is the “lower bound” of a confidence interval?
A 95% confidence interval represents:
options: The probability that the sample mean lies in this interval
The range of sample means expected in 95% of samples
A set of plausible population mean values based on the data
The range where most data points fall

response.prompt: Where is the lower bound of the confidence interval shown in the graph below? ![What is the lower confidence bound](tve-learning-summer/assets/lowerCI.png)

The questions in the next section cover concepts that have not yet been formally taught in this course. Please use what you have learned so far in this class to attempt these more challenging questions. Even if you are unsure of your answer, we encourage you to make your best attempt based on your current understanding.
1. A researcher draws a sample from a city and calculates a 95% confidence interval based on the sample. The 95% confidence interval for the mean income of people in a city is [$45,000, $55,000].

a. A student says: “Based on this sample, there is a 95% chance that the true population mean lies between $45,000 and $55,000.”

Is this interpretation correct or not?
a-i. Explain your reasoning to the previous question.

b. Is $40,000 a plausible value for the population mean of income based on this confidence interval?
Explain your reasoning.
c. Instead of using a confidence level of 95%, the researchers decided to use a confidence level of 90% , what happens with this change?
options: The confidence interval will not change

response.prompt: c-i. Explain your reasoning to the previous question.
d. In order to construct a 90% confidence interval, would the researcher use a z score that is larger than 1.96 or smaller than 1.96?
d-i. Explain your reasoning to the previous question.
2. A researcher collects a random sample of 64 students and finds a sample mean study time of 12 hours per week. The 95% confidence interval is [10, 14].
a. Interpret this 95% confidence interval.
b. What is the margin of error for this confidence interval?

c. Suppose the researcher collects a larger sample of students, resulting in a standard error that is half as large as before. Keeping the confidence level to 95%, would the new confidence interval be wider or narrower than [10, 14]?
options: The new confidence interval will be wider than [10, 14]
The new confidence interval will be narrower than [10, 14]
There is not enough information to make this judgement

In this study, we, a research team from the Educational Psychology Department at UW-Madison (see our lab info here: http://www.icyzhang.com/bk_28250304.html), are interested in understanding how to better teach difficult statistics concepts such as the confidence interval.

This is 2 x 3 experiment, and you were randomly assigned to one of the six conditions. We hypothesized that the embodied videos might be beneficial only if students have embodied prior knowledge.

Here, we provide the link to the main intervention videos. Feel free to take a look if you are interested in what the other group sees.

Embodied: https://vimeo.com/1180350861

Static visual: https://vimeo.com/1180352988

If you have any questions about this study or want to get involved with educational psychology research related to statistics and data science education, please contact Dr. Icy Zhang at icy.zhang@wisc.edu
